## The problem

Our twelve-person team is losing days every sprint to merge pain, and it's getting worse.

- Feature branches routinely live two to four weeks, and by the time we merge, main has drifted enough that "integration" means a half-day of conflict resolution and re-testing.
- Bugs surface only at merge time, when the context that would make them cheap to fix has evaporated, so senior engineers re-derive decisions instead of shipping new work.

## The proposal

Switch to trunk-based development: everyone commits to main at least daily, behind feature flags when work is incomplete, with CI gating every merge.

- Feature flags decouple "merged" from "released," so incomplete work stays invisible to users without blocking teammates from building on top of it.
- A stricter CI gate — fast automated tests plus mandatory review within two hours — becomes our new safety net in place of branch isolation.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is real: without long-lived branches, half-finished features live directly in main, and a careless flag can leak broken functionality to production or silently entangle unrelated work. Teams that adopt trunk-based development without disciplined flag hygiene don't eliminate risk, they just trade merge-conflict pain for a messier main branch and accidental exposure. That's a legitimate cost, not a strawman, and we shouldn't pretend otherwise. To manage it, we'd need a flag-naming convention, a designated owner for every flag, and a weekly review to kill stale ones — without that discipline, this becomes a liability rather than a fix.

- To de-risk the transition, we'll pilot with one squad for a month before rolling out team-wide, so we can validate that our flag discipline actually holds before betting the whole team on it.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
